transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Yeah… I guess I’m here because I’ve just been feeling low for a long time. I still do my routes, get through work, and I help out with volunteer shifts too—funny, the guys there always joke I’m the reliable one, like my old truck that somehow keeps running even when it shouldn’t—but inside it’s like this heaviness is there most days.

I’m doing what I’m supposed to do, you know, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Like I’m present, but not really in my own life.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to look forward to?

I don’t know… I mean, I still do things. Like, if there’s a cookout at the volunteer place, I’ll show up, help set up tables, talk with people some. I used to mess around with fixing up my truck on weekends—though honestly half the time that thing is held together by luck and old bolts.

But as far as looking forward to stuff… I’m not sure. I don’t really think about it that way. I mostly just do what’s on the calendar or what needs doing, you know?

Can you think back to the last time you genuinely looked forward to something or felt a sense of enjoyment in doing it—like when you used to fix up your truck? Did that feeling fade, or does it still come up at all?

I’m not sure I can put my finger on the last time, honestly. I mean, the truck… I still mess with it sometimes, but half the time it’s because something’s rattling or leaking and I don’t want to pay a shop, you know?

There are moments, maybe, where I’m kind of absorbed in it—like finding the right part or getting the engine to turn over after fighting with it for an hour—but I don’t know if I’d call that looking forward to it. It’s more like… I just do it.

And then I get sidetracked anyway. Last time I was out there, my neighbor came over talking about his mower, and somehow we ended up discussing old carburetors for twenty minutes. So, yeah… enjoyment, I guess it comes up here and there, but it’s hard for me to say when I really felt excited about something.
Would you say that activities you used to enjoy, like fixing up your truck or spending time with people, no longer feel rewarding or satisfying to you — even when you do them?

I don’t know if I’d say “no longer,” exactly. That sounds kind of… final, you know?

Sometimes I get something out of it, I guess. Like if the truck starts after I’ve been messing with it, there’s a little “well, okay, I did that” feeling. But then again, last week I went out just to check one noise and ended up reorganizing a coffee can full of bolts for half an hour because I couldn’t find the right size. My dad used to keep bolts like that too, all mixed together, drove my mom crazy.

With people, same thing. I show up, I talk, I laugh if somebody says something funny. I’m not sitting there thinking, “this is rewarding” or anything. I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether it feels satisfying. It’s more like… I do it, and then it’s done.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or low for most of the day, even if you’re doing things and interacting with people?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still get up and do my routes, talk to customers, go over to the volunteer place when I said I would. So from the outside I probably look like I’m keeping up fine.

But most days there’s this… heavy, low kind of feeling just sitting on me. Like I’m moving through the day because that’s what you do, not because I’m really in it. Even if I’m talking to people or getting things done, it’s still kind of there underneath.
Do you find that you feel tired or like you don’t have much energy, even when you haven’t done anything particularly hard or strenuous?

I don’t know… I mean, I get tired like anybody else. Driving around all day, getting in and out, dealing with people—that can wear you down, even if it’s not like digging ditches or anything.

But if you mean just sitting there and feeling wiped out for no good reason, I’m not sure. Some days I’ll get home and kind of sit in the truck for a minute before going inside, but then I start thinking about whether I left the cooler in the back or if I need gas in the morning, and next thing I know I’m checking receipts.

So… maybe a little, but I haven’t really kept track of it. It’s hard for me to say whether it’s tired-tired or just normal end-of-the-day stuff.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or low for the majority of the day, even when nothing particularly bad is happening?

Yeah… most days, I’d say so. It’s kind of why I came in, honestly. I can still do my routes, and I show up for the volunteer shifts when I said I would, but there’s this heavy, low feeling that’s just… there.

Even if nothing bad happened that day, I’m still sort of moving through it like I’m on autopilot. Like I’m doing the steps, talking to people, making deliveries, whatever needs doing, but I don’t feel like I’m really in my own life, if that makes sense.
Would you say that most days, your low mood is present for nearly the entire day, even when things are going okay or there’s no clear reason for it?

Yeah… I know I kind of keep circling back to the same thing, but yes. That’s really why I came in.

I’ll be doing my route, stopping at the same places, talking to the same people—there’s this one guy who always wants to tell me about his lawn, every single time—and I can talk and nod and do what I’m supposed to do. Same with the volunteer shifts, I show up and I’m useful enough.

But underneath it, most days, there’s this heavy, low feeling just sitting there. Even when nothing’s wrong exactly. It’s like I’m going through the motions more than actually being in my own life.
Would you say that you often feel tired or low on energy even on days when you haven’t done much physically or emotionally taxing?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of worn out, but then I start thinking, well, did I actually do less that day, or was I still running errands, answering calls, dealing with traffic… you know how it adds up.

Like even a “quiet” day, I’ll notice I’ve still been in and out of the truck, stopping for gas, checking on stuff. And then I get home and sit down and it’s hard to tell if I’m low on energy or just… done with the day.

So I guess I haven’t really noticed it clearly enough to say yes. It’s not something I’ve been keeping track of.
Would you say that your low mood is present nearly every day, and that it lasts throughout most of the day, even when things are going okay?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s fair to say. I know I’ve kind of answered it already, but that’s really the thing that made me come in.

I can get through my routes and do my volunteer shifts, and from the outside I probably look like I’m doing what I’m supposed to. I mean, I’ll be driving around, making stops, talking to people about whatever—sometimes the same small talk over and over, you know—and I keep moving.

But most days there’s this heavy, low feeling sitting on me. It’s there even when the day is going okay. Like nothing has to happen for it to show up. I’m just going through the motions more than really feeling like I’m in my own life.
Can you recall if there have been days when you didn’t feel like doing anything at all, even things that used to bring you a sense of satisfaction or pleasure?

I don’t know if I can pin that down exactly. There are days I don’t feel like doing much, sure, but then I get caught up thinking, well, nobody really feels like doing chores or making calls or running around town.

As far as things that used to feel satisfying… I’m not sure. Like with the volunteer thing, sometimes I show up and I’m fine once I’m there, and other times I’m mostly thinking about getting through it. But that could just be the day, or being busy, or whatever.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to it in that way—whether I’m not wanting to do anything at all, or just not wanting to start.
Would you say that your low mood is something you feel almost every day, and that it sticks around for most of the day, even when things are going fine?

Yeah… I know I’m kind of circling the same answer, but yes, that’s what I mean. It’s there most days.

Like I can be out on my route, doing the stops, talking to somebody at a counter, or later going to a volunteer shift, and everything might be going fine on paper. No big problem happened. But inside it’s like this heavy, low feeling is just sitting there with me.

Sometimes I’ll catch myself thinking, I’m doing all the things I’m supposed to be doing, but I don’t really feel like I’m in it. More like I’m just moving through the day because that’s what you do. So yeah, I’d say it sticks around a lot of the day, even when things are okay.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling this way — with a low mood most days, even when things are okay — for at least two years now?

Yeah… at least two years, yes. I’d say it’s been more like about three years now.

It kind of started after my father died. I mean, I know people lose parents and you’re supposed to grieve and all that, and he and I weren’t even the type to have these big emotional talks—he was more, you know, “just get the job done” kind of guy. I catch myself thinking about little things, like his old tools or the way he’d complain about traffic, and then I realize how long it’s been.

But yeah, to answer what you asked, this low feeling has been going on since around then, so about three years.
